title: Open restriction and adjunction transport through actual completion units
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $B_{n,T}=(A_n)_T$ and $\widehat R_T=\lim_nB_{n,T}$. Use the strict semilinear module-system category $\mathscr S_T$, derived reduction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$, and the actual unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Completeness means the quotient-tower Roos-triangle condition of [def-weil-derived-complete], and normalized means that every transition-adjoint $N_m\otimes^L_{B_{m,T}}B_{n,T}\to N_n$ is invertible for $m\ge n$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Identify $j^{-1}\widehat R_X=\widehat R_U$ and $j^{-1}B_{n,X}=B_{n,U}$. Write $j_!\dashv j^*$ for exact localized ringed-site extension and restriction, $J_j\dashv P_j$ for their termwise-system adjunctions, and $\eta^o,\epsilon^o,\eta^S,\epsilon^S$ for the respective units and counits [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

Assume that $j_!$ preserves quotient-complete objects and that the actual $u_P$ is invertible on every quotient-complete object on $U$ and $X$, while $e_N$ is invertible on normalized systems and $\mathcal L_TN$ is complete for such $N$. Supply a natural isomorphism $r_K:\mathcal R_Xj_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\mathcal R_UK$ represented simultaneously on flat-term K-flat complexes by the canonical open tensor maps $[x]\otimes a\mapsto[x\otimes a|_U]$, commuting with strict quotient transitions and scalar-unit augmentations [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

Ordinary restriction $j^*$ preserves quotient completeness and agrees with completed restriction, including its actual completion comparison and finite projections [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison]. Restriction of the quotient tensor models defines a natural strict-system isomorphism
$$s_H:\mathcal R_Uj^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}P_j\mathcal R_XH.$$
For every complete $K$ on $U$ and complete $H$ on $X$, the following are equalities of the specified simultaneous derived system transformations:
$$P_j(r_K)\circ s_{j_!K}\circ\mathcal R_U(\eta^o_K)=\eta^S_{\mathcal R_UK},$$
$$\mathcal R_X(\epsilon^o_H)=\epsilon^S_{\mathcal R_XH}\circ J_j(s_H)\circ r_{j^*H}.$$
Define
$$d_K=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_X(r_K^{-1}),\qquad
 b_H=u_{j^*H}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_U(s_H^{-1}).$$
These are natural isomorphisms, and their normalization and realized-adjunction equations are
$$r_K\circ\mathcal R_X(d_K)=e_{J_j\mathcal R_UK},$$
$$b_{j_!K}\circ\mathcal L_U(P_j(r_K^{-1}))\circ\mathcal L_U(\eta^S_{\mathcal R_UK})\circ u_K=\eta^o_K,$$
$$u_H^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_X(\epsilon^S_{\mathcal R_XH})\circ\mathcal L_X(J_j(s_H))\circ d_{j^*H}^{-1}=\epsilon^o_H.$$
In particular $d$ and $b$ identify the realized open adjunction with the localized ringed-site adjunction. The equalities hold before evaluating the systems, and use the actual adjunction units, counits and transposes rather than arbitrary reconstruction isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model] with the given open immersion and coefficient rings. It supplies, for a flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to K$, the flat-term K-flat representative $j_!Q\to j_!K$ and the chain isomorphism $r_Q$ of strict semilinear systems. Its formula is $[x]\otimes a\mapsto[x\otimes a|_U]$; its quotient-transition and scalar-unit squares commute before localization. Its localization is the specified natural $r_K$ and is independent of $Q$. No completeness or quasi-compactness is needed for this step.

proof.text:
An open immersion is a locally closed immersion with identity closed factor. Apply [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison] to $j$. Its coefficient isomorphisms are those fixed in the statement. It gives exact ordinary restriction, preservation of quotient completeness, and invertibility of the specified ordinary-to-completed comparison, with its completion-unit and finite-projection compatibilities. To realize the finite comparisons simultaneously, choose a flat-term K-flat representative $F$ of $H$ in the reduction calculus. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $j^*F$ is again flat-term K-flat. Restriction of tensor sections gives
$$ (j^*F)\otimes_{\widehat R_U}B_{n,U}\ \cong\ j^*(F\otimes_{\widehat R_X}B_{n,X}). $$
On an object of the localized site both sides send $x\otimes a$ to the same $x\otimes a$. Therefore the squares for $B_m\to B_n$ and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ commute on complexes. These assemble to an isomorphism of strict systems, not merely separate evaluated arrows. The simultaneous scalar-extension and localization construction of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] gives its natural localization $s_H:\mathcal R_Uj^*H\cong P_j\mathcal R_XH$. These are exactly the inverses of the finite comparisons in the immersion lemma, so they retain its finite-projection and completion compatibilities.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 and Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); the cited immersion lemma supplies the completed comparison, not Tag 0GL1 alone.

proof.text:
For the reduced unit equation use the same representative $Q$ as in Step 1 and its extension $j_!Q$. The open unit is normalized by the identity on sections on the open [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Thus on the localized site the composite
$$P_j(r_Q)\circ s_{j_!Q}\circ\mathcal R_U(\eta^o_Q)$$
sends $x\otimes a$ to the same section $x\otimes a$ of $P_jJ_j\mathcal R_UQ$. This is precisely the termwise-system unit $\eta^S_{\mathcal R_UQ}$. The comparison of Step 1 and the restriction comparison of Step 2 commute with all quotient transitions, so this is an equality of chain maps of strict systems. By [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], the open-system adjunction is the termwise open adjunction and its simultaneous derived units and transposes are induced by these maps. Localizing the chain-map equality proves
$$P_j(r_K)\circ s_{j_!K}\circ\mathcal R_U(\eta^o_K)=\eta^S_{\mathcal R_UK}$$
in the derived system category; it does not use faithfulness of evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 and sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I, using the specified open-unit normalization and simultaneous system adjunction of the cited nodes; explicit generator calculation.

proof.text:
For the counit use the flat-term K-flat $F$ of Step 2. Its restriction and then extension are flat-term K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and [lem-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model]. On the extension-presheaf summand indexed by a map into $U$, the localized ringed-site counit sends $[x]$ to its ambient section $x$. Hence reduction of this counit sends $[x]\otimes a$ to $x\otimes a$. The other composite sends $[x]\otimes a$ first by $r_{j^*F}$ to $[x\otimes a|_U]$, then by $J_j(s_F)$ to that same restricted tensor section, and finally by the termwise counit to $x\otimes a$. These are equal additive, scalar-compatible maps on every presheaf summand, hence after sheafification and in each complex degree. The maps commute with every quotient transition. The termwise adjunction and its derived localization in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] therefore give the equality of system transformations
$$\mathcal R_X(\epsilon^o_H)=\epsilon^S_{\mathcal R_XH}\circ J_j(s_H)\circ r_{j^*H}.$$
The equality is induced before localization, not inferred from equal evaluations.

proof.text: For complete $K,H$, the assumed preservation of completeness by $j_!$ and Step 2 give completeness of $j_!K$ and $j^*H$. Thus the actual units $u_{j_!K}$ and $u_{j^*H}$ are invertible by the hypotheses. Define $d_K=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_X(r_K^{-1})$ and $b_H=u_{j^*H}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_U(s_H^{-1})$. Each factor is an isomorphism. The naturality of $u$ in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], together with that of $r,s$, gives naturality of their inverses and these composites. All the units used here are the specified units of $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$.

source.place: Agent formal calculation using the actual adjunction supplied by the cited node (resolution/limit foundations: Tags 06YS and 0941).

proof.text:
Write $A=j_!K$ and $N=J_j\mathcal R_UK$. The triangle identity in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] reads $e_{\mathcal R_XA}\circ\mathcal R_X(u_A)=1$, so invertibility of $u_A$ gives $\mathcal R_X(u_A^{-1})=e_{\mathcal R_XA}$. Naturality of $e$ for $r_K:\mathcal R_XA\to N$ now gives
$$\begin{aligned}
r_K\circ\mathcal R_X(d_K)
&=r_K\circ e_{\mathcal R_XA}\circ\mathcal R_X\mathcal L_X(r_K^{-1})\\
&=e_N\circ\mathcal R_X\mathcal L_X(r_K)\circ\mathcal R_X\mathcal L_X(r_K^{-1})=e_N.
\end{aligned}$$
This proves the normalization equation directly in $D(\mathscr S_X)$.

source.place: Agent formal calculation: naturality of the actual counit and the adjunction triangle identity; cited node, system-adjunction paragraph.

proof.text:
For the realized unit, Step 3 rearranges to
$$s_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ P_j(r_K^{-1})\circ\eta^S_{\mathcal R_UK}=\mathcal R_U(\eta^o_K).$$
Substitute the definition of $b_{j_!K}$ in the proposed equation and use functoriality of $\mathcal L_U$. Its left side becomes
$$u_{j^*j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_U\mathcal R_U(\eta^o_K)\circ u_K=\eta^o_K.$$
The equality is the naturality square of the actual unit $u$ for $\eta^o_K$, as supplied by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Both $K$ and $j^*j_!K$ are complete, so the displayed inverses are defined.
